solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Back-up cop's first to stop fight in tour of boozers

indicators.note: back as a verb tells us to run the word up in the other direction
a letter set to stop a fight sits plugging the middle of it

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word cop's

explanation.surface: A police officer calling for back-up to break up a scuffle during an evening of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-up' looks like reinforcements, but 'Back' just signals a reversal; 'to stop' means plug the inside. Boozers are British slang for pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is an outing moving from one drinking establishment to the next, hence a tour of boozers.

clue.text: Plebs regularly consumed revolting old Spanish bread

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of Plebs
revolting, in a down clue, turns the eating word upside down

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Common people ate disgusting old Spanish loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency of Spain before the euro; bread is slang for money.

clue.text: British pasty shortage's rising, something quite unpredictable

indicators.note: rising, in a down entry, lifts the shortage piece up above the pasty piece

parts.note: wan means pale or pasty
lacks, as lack is, a shortage

explanation.surface: A news item about a shortage of British pasties getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' works only because this is a down entry: the shortage piece climbs above the pasty piece. 'pasty' looks like the Cornish pie but means pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A black swan is a rare, unforeseeable event with large consequences, a term popularised by Nassim Taleb.

clue.text: Voluminous jumper belonging to me

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
my means belonging to me

explanation.surface: A baggy jumper, the woollen kind, that is mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater; it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means spacious, with plenty of capacity, so voluminous.

clue.text: US novelist who pens things creative and new

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the creative piece sits inside who

parts.note: art covers creative works

explanation.surface: An American author who writes inventive, original work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing, fitting a novelist, but here means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Wharton wrote The Age of Innocence and was an American author.

clue.text: Set off in boat after Anglo-Saxon attack

indicators.note: after places the boating piece behind the Anglo-Saxon abbreviation

parts.note: to sail is to set off by boat

explanation.surface: Raiders launch their boats to strike, like Anglo-Saxons arriving by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to set upon violently, a straight synonym of the verb attack.

clue.text: Scoff rudely at the pigs

definitions.note: scoff is British slang for food, a noun here

indicators.note: rudely indicates the letters of at the pigs are roughly reordered

explanation.surface: Someone jeering impolitely at pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' reads as a verb (jeer) but is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a pasta dish, an example of food or grub.

clue.text: Adult and juvenile cat start to attack dog

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
a kit, or kitten, is a young cat

indicators.note: start to takes only the opening letter of attack

explanation.surface: A grown cat and a kitten about to go for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large Japanese breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: I slipped out of underwear — duke was reluctant to leave

indicators.note: the I sheds the underwear, so it is removed from that word

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear

explanation.surface: An undressing scene in which a duke lingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipped out of' removes the second I from LINGERIE, leaving LINGERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay on and delay departing, so lingered fits the past-tense phrase.

clue.text: One swam dubiously around a mermaid

indicators.note: around tells us the shuffled letters wrap about the a
dubiously signals the letters of one swam are in a questionable, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Someone swimming oddly near a mermaid, as if a sailor's tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubiously' turns ONE SWAM into SEWOMAN; 'around' puts A inside it after SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea-woman is an old term for a female creature of the ocean, so a mermaid.

clue.text: Ultimately con one in a hundred people

indicators.note: ultimately takes only the final letter of the word con
in places the single numeral inside the hundred

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A con artist cheating one person in every hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a people sharing a country and identity; the word can mean a whole populace.

clue.text: Origins of lacrosse, unpleasantly dangerous ball game

indicators.note: origins means the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: Lacrosse began as a rough, dangerous ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Temperature satisfactory for wine

parts.note: okay means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A wine served at an acceptable temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine from the Tokaj region.

clue.text: Finger and foot briefly make contact

parts.note: to finger something is to touch it
the foot of something is its base

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a quick touch of hand and foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch base is an idiom for checking in with someone for a short conversation.

clue.text: 10 politicians we'd enjoy locking up

definitions.note: refers to the answer to 10 across, nation; Sweden is one

indicators.note: the words politicians we'd enjoy hold the answer imprisoned within them

explanation.surface: A wish to see politicians jailed, which the public would relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locking up' hides the answer across politiciaNS WE'D ENjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian country, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Chewed nut, dreary fare

indicators.note: chewed means mashed up, so the letters of nut and dreary are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull meal of chewed nuts, food as fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like food; it is a ticket. A day return is a British rail ticket out and back the same day.
explanation.definitionFit: A day return is a type of travel ticket, and a fare is what a passenger pays for one.

clue.text: Defeated United 1-0 to move into first place

indicators.note: the zero is told to shift to the front of the assembled letters

parts.note: Utd is the usual abbreviation for United in football results
the score is read as the word one followed by the letter O for zero

explanation.surface: A football report: United's one-nil win lifts them to the top of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: UTD + ONE + O gives UTDONEO; 'to move into first place' brings the final O to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outdone is to be beaten or surpassed, so defeated.

clue.text: Respond too strongly with regard to damaged crate

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: damaged shows the letters of crate are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone getting too upset about a broken crate.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to show an excessive emotional or physical response.

clue.text: Drinking cups reach Alice Springs stores

indicators.note: stores means holds within, so the answer is kept inside reach Alice Springs

explanation.surface: Goblets arriving at the shops in Alice Springs, an Australian outback town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' hides the answer in reaCH ALICES Springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalices are goblets, especially those used for wine in church.

clue.text: Flattering Henry, wealthy but not married

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: not tells us the married abbreviation is dropped from the wealthy word

parts.note: moneyed means wealthy

explanation.surface: A rich bachelor called Henry described in sweet terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeyed words are sweet and ingratiating, so flattering.

clue.text: Leaving university, coming out in negative financial state

indicators.note: leaving means the university letter departs from the coming-out word

parts.note: a debut is a first appearance or coming out

explanation.surface: A graduate leaving university in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: Debt is owing money, a balance below zero.

clue.text: One pillaging cases of Rioja imported by monarch

indicators.note: the cases of each word are its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A king having Spanish wine shipped in crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases of' takes the outer letters of both 'Rioja' and 'imported'; 'by' just sets ER beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider is someone who plunders or loots during an attack.

clue.text: Great eccentric cheers boat race

indicators.note: eccentric signals that the letters of great are set out oddly

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: An odd person shouting encouragement at a rowing race.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting event made up of boat or yacht races.

clue.text: Sentimental drunk embraced by society's outsiders

indicators.note: embraced by tells us the drunk is hugged by the outer letters
outsiders are the first and last letters of society's

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A tearful drunk taken in by society's misfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Slushy describes something mawkish and excessively emotional.

clue.text: Minor offender nibbled Cockney's ear, says Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swaps the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: a Cockney says bit 'er for bit her, dropping the h
lug is slang for an ear

explanation.surface: A minor scuffle in which someone bit a woman's ear, reported in Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney 'bit 'er lug' (bit her ear) becomes LITTER BUG when the initial B and L are swapped; Cockneys are working-class Londoners known for dropping H.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug drops rubbish in public, a small-scale wrongdoer.

clue.text: Head of Tech and associate are in agreement

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of Tech

parts.note: an ally is an associate

explanation.surface: A tech boss and colleague see eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that tally correspond, the verb meaning to match or agree.

clue.text: Danger for every single Liberal

parts.note: per means for each
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A warning that every single Liberal is a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is a synonym of danger, serious risk of harm.

clue.text: Haughty professional nude discarding clothes

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: the outer letters of nude, its covering, are stripped off

explanation.surface: A professional nude model too superior to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean arrogant or self-important, the sense of haughty.

clue.text: Skin problem? Give us a ring!

definitions.meaning: split as ..., a request to telephone

explanation.surface: A dermatology clinic's advert inviting patients to phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A callus is thickened skin from friction; read as two words it means phone us.

clue.text: Seats intemperate old chap next to son

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive or intemperate
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Furniture for an excessive old fellow and his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottomans are low upholstered seats or footstools without backs.

clue.text: Adage remaining timeless

indicators.note: timeless is read as time-less, asking for the remaining word without its T for time

parts.note: staying means remaining

explanation.surface: An old saying that stays true forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' is read as time-less: STAYING loses T, the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A saying is a proverb or maxim, which is what an adage is.

clue.text: Bishop and setter have a go at brigand- age

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the setter refers to herself as I
to try is to have a go

explanation.surface: A bishop and the setter attempting a crime, with brigandage split to look like a period.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is robbery by outlaws, the activity that brigandage names.
